docs.title: epc_nondomestic: column provenance
docs.text:
Where every column of the table epc_nondomestic comes from, what was done to it, how it is checked and why. Generated from the metadata of uprn-epc-nondomestic version 0.1.0 at commit b49a661.

The table holds every certificate of the Scottish Government's extended historic extract of non-domestic Energy Performance Certificates, release 2026Q3, one row per certificate, values exactly as published, with typed copies for joining a cohort by UPRN and date. The table itself is private; this site holds no value of any row, no address and no postcode.

  • Columns: 57 pages, one per column.
  • Pinned sources: the 5 files the build reads or hashes.
  • Decisions: the 18 decisions, in force and history.
  • Checks: what every check family tests and how far it reaches.

The data dictionary, the loader, the join queries and the build record are in the repository. The sibling table of domestic certificates is uprn-epc.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text: Every check the build can emit, by family (epc_nd_ingest/check_catalogue.yaml). Each is blocking: a failure stops the build and nothing is promoted. A build's manifest records which were emitted and their results; this page defines them and says how far each reaches.

docs.title: source.member
docs.text:
Name pattern ^source\.[^/]+/extracted/[^/]+\.csv$. The extract's SHA256 equals the pin in sources.yaml, so the bytes read are the bytes reviewed.

Applies to every column. Coverage: every byte of the file. Runs in every build.

docs.text:

docs.text:

docs.text:

docs.title: Derived columns
docs.text: Column Type Nullable Description rrn text yes The report reference number as published where not empty, NULL where empty (126 rows). Unique where present. uprn_sepcr 64-bit integer no The register's own 10-digit number for the building, trimmed and as an integer. Not the Gazetteer UPRN. Present in every row. uprn_osg 64-bit integer yes The One Scotland Gazetteer UPRN as an integer, NULL where the published cell is empty (35.4% of rows). The only column a UPRN join compares. A padded cohort UPRN matches once cast to bigint. pc_norm text yes POSTCODE in upper case with every space and tab removed. NULL where nothing is left. Nothing repaired. The postcode join normalises the cohort postcode by the same rule. datazone_2001 text yes The 2001 data zone code when DATA_ZONE starts with S01 and six digits followed by a space or the end, otherwise NULL. datazone_2001_status text no code, empty, not_a_datazone (for 00QQMB and the like) or unknown_code (well formed, not in the pinned list. The build fails if any). datazone_2011 text yes The 2011 data zone code by the same rule, otherwise NULL. datazone_2011_status text no As datazone_2001_status, for the 2011 column. inspection_date_parsed date no INSPECTION_DATE (yyyy-mm-dd) as a date: the day the assessor saw the building. The dated joins choose the certificate by it. Outliers (2002 to 2108) are kept as published. A value that does not parse stops the build. lodgement_date_parsed date no LODGEMENT_DATE (yyyy-mm-dd) as a date. The administrative date of the certificate, a median of 8 days after the inspection. The ten-year validity runs from it. created_at_parsed timestamp no CREATED_AT (dd/mm/yyyy hh:mm:ss) as a timestamp to the second: when the certificate was lodged on the register. Never later than the last day of the release quarter. historic_flag flag no 1 where HISTORIC is True (the certificate has been superseded), 0 where False. Any other value stops the build. floor_area_int 32-bit integer no The conditioned floor area of the building in square metres as an integer, 4 to 138,037 in this release. Shared with dwellings in unit, not in what is measured. current_energy_performance_rating_int 32-bit integer no The current energy performance rating as an integer: calculated emissions in kg of CO2 per square metre per year, lower is better, negative allowed. Not the domestic rating, which scores energy cost and where higher is better. potential_energy_performance_rating_num decimal(19,4) yes The potential energy performance rating (kg of CO2 per square metre per year after the listed improvements) as decimal(19,4). NULL exactly where the published text is 'Data removed' (1,712 rows). building_emissions_num decimal(19,4) no The Building Emission Rate (kg of CO2 per square metre per year) as decimal(19,4). The same quantity as the domestic emissions per floor area. primary_energy_value_int 32-bit integer no The primary energy indicator (kWh per square metre per year) as an integer. The same quantity as the domestic primary energy indicator.

docs.title: join-by-inspection-date
docs.text:
Decided 2026-11-14. Status: in_force.

Decision. The dated joins choose the certificate with the latest inspection_date_parsed on or before the cohort date and return the inspection and lodgement dates, the age in days from the inspection, and a flag for a lodgement before its inspection. The undated join returns the current certificate. No query decides expiry and no query reads the clock.

Why. Carried over from uprn-epc. The inspection is when the assessor saw the building. In 2026Q3 lodgement follows it by a median of 8 days, by 31 to 365 days in 17,125 certificates and by over a year in 1,411, and precedes it in 195, so both dates are returned.

docs.title: join-output-own-columns
docs.text:
Decided 2026-11-14. Status: in_force.

Decision. Each of the three queries has its own output. A column that does not apply to a query is not returned by it. The non-domestic measurements are returned under their own names, with the three quantities shared with dwellings. The undated query returns no cohort_date, epc_age_days, historic_flag or tie column.

Why. uprn-epc's queries select domestic columns that do not exist here, and the domestic and non-domestic ratings measure different things (reviews of 14 November 2026). The undated query takes no date, returns the current certificate and has no tie rule.

Decision. The registry names exactly one member, identified by its file. The check that replaces uprn-epc's file-year rule is that no CREATED_AT is later than the last day of the release quarter, which the registry records as quarter_end.

docs.title: postcode-join-ranks-before-it-compares
docs.text:
Decided 2026-11-14. Status: in_force.

Decision. The postcode join answers which buildings were at the postcode as of the cohort date. For each building with any certificate at the cohort postcode it chooses the latest eligible certificate over all the building's postcodes, then returns the building only if that certificate carries the cohort postcode. A cohort row whose postcode has certificates by the date, all on buildings whose latest certificate carries another postcode, gets no_building_at_postcode_by_date.

Why. 258 register numbers carry two or more postcodes over their certificates. Filtering by postcode before ranking, as uprn-epc's query does, returns a building at its old postcode with its older certificate. As of 30 September 2026 that would return 262 building and postcode pairs that the building's latest certificate contradicts (review of 14 November 2026).

Decided 2026-11-14. Status: in_force.

Typed copies exist for the identifiers, the three dates, the superseded flag, the floor area, the current rating, the potential rating, the building emission rate and the primary energy value. docs.title: width-is-accepted-length
docs.text:
Decided 2026-11-14. Status: in_force.

Decision. Every text column has an integer width, the longest value the build accepts, from the measured longest value and the next bucket. The buckets end at 8,000. Widths and lengths are counted in UTF-16 code units, as SQL Server counts an nvarchar, so a character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane counts as two. SQL Server stores a column as nvarchar(width) when the width is up to 4,000 and as nvarchar(max) above. The row digest converts the first operand of each concatenation chunk to nvarchar(max).

Why. IMPROVEMENT_RECOMMENDATIONS reaches 4,451 characters and 3 cells pass 4,000, the most a bounded nvarchar holds, and the value must stay as published. Keeping the width an integer keeps the schema check for every column, this one included. uprn-epc's rule of no nvarchar(max) rested on a longest value of 3,330 characters and cannot hold here. The unit is SQL Server's because a count of characters would accept a value that does not fit its column (implementation review of 14 November 2026). Release 2026Q3 holds no character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane, so the two counts agree for it.
